title: 1958 AHSME Problem 14
statement: At a dance party a group of boys and girls exchange dances as follows: one boy dances with \(5\) girls, a second boy dances with \(6\) girls, and so on, the last boy dancing with all the girls. If \(b\) represents the number of boys and \(g\) the number of girls, then:

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
It is impossible to determine a relation between \(b\) and
\(g\) without knowing \(b+g\)

solutions.text:
The last of the \(b\) terms in the sequence \(5,6,7,\ldots\) is \[ 5+(b-1)=b+4. \] This last number equals the total number \(g\) of girls. Hence \(g=b+4,\) or \(b=g-4.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The numbers of partners form the sequence \(5,6,7,\ldots,g\)
There are \(b\) terms, so express the last term using the arithmetic-sequence formula
